# Ype! Writer (`dsh-ype-writer`)

> [!Tip]
>
> 中文版见 README_zh_CN.md。
A DSH article auditor that scores an article paragraph by paragraph against a `rule.toml`. Every rul
e opens its own LLM session, so the scoring standard is reproducible, reviewable, and committable.
- **Audience / anti-audience**: two independent sessions score audience fit and anti-audience legibi

lity, from which a measured "pandering index" is derived and compared with the target.
- **One sessi
on per rule**: anti-patterns, don'ts, and requirements each run in their own session; `llm = N` runs

replicas and averages them.
- **Script rules**: Python functions for deterministic checks; no token

s spent.
- **No runtime dependencies**: the TOML parser ships with the package; nothing extra to ins
tall into a profile.
## Install and load
Requirements:

- DSH with the plugin manager available (the `plugin_manager` tool or Creator mode)
- Node.js 20 or

newer
- Python 3 only if you use script or filter rules

1. Open **Plugins** in the sidebar and click **Add plugin**.
2. Enter `https://github.com/catilgrass

3. Click **Install** and wait for "Installed".
### Ask an agent
Paste this into a session that can use the plugin manager (Creator mode, or full access):
> Install the DSH bundle from https://github.com/catilgrass/ype-writer into this profile with `plugi
n_manager` (`install_bundle`), then confirm `ype_check` appears in the tool list and `ype-writer` in
the skill catalog. Finish with a smoke check: `ype_check(template: "tutorial-guide", text: "This is
g. Finish with a smoke check: `ype_check(template: "tutorial-guide", text: "This is a smoke test.")`
The loader hot-loads the bundle, so `ype_check` appears in every session using that profile, and the
`ype-writer` skill joins the skill catalog when the profile has one. Working from a local checkout?
Use `target` with the absolute path instead, and reinstall after edits.
## Use
[代码示例省略，未执行]
| Argument   | Required             | Meaning
equired             | Meaning                                                                      |
| `rule`     | one of rule/template | Path to the rule file, absolute or relative to the session wor

king directory |
| `template` | one of rule/template | Bundled template name such as `health-science

` or `zh_CN/health-science`     |
| `text`     | one of text/path     | Full article text

|
| `path`     | one of text/path     | Path to the
article file                                                     |
The tool returns a Markdown report (`value.report`) plus structured per-paragraph and per-rule resul
ts for programmatic use. The report keeps every rule's raw score so the final score can be recompute
for programmatic use. The report keeps every rule's raw score so the final score can be recomputed.
Try it on this README:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
### Visual report
The browser half renders a card after each `ype_check` with the score, paragraph count, and warning
count; "Open report" selects the **Article Review Report** panel, which draws the score ring, per-pa
ragraph score bars, the rule table, and warnings. Card and panel read one structured projection (`pr
esentationMeta`), so opening the panel costs no extra Host call.
If this version added the client half while DSH was already running, restart the DSH process once: t
he client module registry caches a package's client declaration for the process lifetime. After the
restart the card appears on the next check.
### Temporary rules
If `rule` points at something that is not valid TOML — a Markdown review spec, a near-miss rule, a b
roken file — the tool turns it into a valid rule: it keeps the requirements the file states (even in
prose or Markdown), repairs a malformed TOML, and infers the rest from the article. The check then
runs with that rule, prints it under "Temporary rule" in the report, and adds a warning saying wheth
er the rule was generated or repaired. The draft is never written to disk. This costs one extra mode
l call (two at most, if the first draft fails validation) and is meant for one-off reviews where com
mitting a rule file is not possible. Disable it with `autoDraftRules: false` in the plugin config.
## Filters
Filters narrow the review to the copy that matters. Each filter is a Python script defining `filter(
text)` that returns only the text to check; the returned string is split into paragraphs once and sh
ared by every session. Comment-only reviews and Markdown stripping use the same contract.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Three selection scripts ship in `filters/`: `comments.py` (only `//` lines), `markdown.py` (prose wi
thout Markdown scaffolding; fence markers dropped, contents kept), and `code.py` (only fenced code).
Reference one by path, relative to the rule file:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Filters run in declared order. A chain that selects nothing fails the check instead of silently scor
ing an empty article, and the report lists which filters ran and how many characters they removed.
## Skill and templates
On load, the plugin registers a `ype-writer` skill with the profile's skill registry (profiles witho
ut a skills service simply get the tool). The skill documents the recommended workflow: **write the
article → copy a template into `rule.toml` → adapt it → run `ype_check` → iterate on the report**, p
lus rule design guidance, how to read the report, and common mistakes.
`templates/` ships eight copy-ready rule templates:
| Template                 | Use for                              | Main guardrails
| `health-science.toml`    | Patient and family health explainers | cure claims, fear, replacing med

ication, pseudoscience |
